children: has issued a strong long-term sales forecast to reach over $63B in annual sales by fiscal year 2030, according to Bloomberg.
Speaking at the company’s annual conference on Wednesday, Chief Operating and Financial Officer Robin Washington outlined the target for the fiscal year ending in January 2030.
The long-term projection easily topped the average analyst consensus of $61.4B compiled by Bloomberg.

As per the report, the optimistic projection comes as Salesforce rebounds from market fears that generative AI tools would displace traditional enterprise software companies. CEO Marc Benioff told attendees that the tech industry is undergoing a massive shift, emphasizing that Salesforce intends to remain at the center of enterprise AI adoption.

The company is already capitalizing on the AI boom. An early investment in AI startup Anthropic yielded a $2.6 billion gain last quarter, with Benioff noting plans to eventually monetize those shares to help fund its $60 billion stock buyback program.

To drive further growth, Salesforce highlighted new integrations including "Claudeforce" which connects company data to Anthropic's Claude and Koa, a new AI reasoning model built on Nvidia architecture currently being tested by nearly 1,000 enterprise clients.
Executives also noted that Slack, acquired in 2021, has rapidly evolved into the company's primary control hub for managing autonomous AI agents.

title: Salesforce expects $63B in revenue by 2030 as AI drives growth
